title: Sikh Empire
capsule: The Sikh Empire was forged by Maharaja Ranjit Singh, who unified the Sikh Misls and was proclaimed maharaja at Lahore on April 12, 1801. At its greatest extent the empire encompassed the Punjab, Kashmir (conquered 1819), Peshawar (1818), and Multan (1818), making it the last major indigenous power to resist British expansion on the subcontinent. Ranjit Singh's death in 1839 unleashed succession conflict and the Anglo-Sikh Wars (1845–46 and 1848–49); the British defeated the Khalsa army at Gujrat on February 21, 1849, and annexed the Punjab by proclamation on March 29, 1849.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Sikh Empire's boundaries are well documented through British survey and treaty records, particularly from the 1840s, with earlier frontier zones in the northwest attested through campaign records and revenue accounts.
